## The Dawn Guard  -  Class Composition

- **Frontline**: Fighter, Paladin, Barbarian, Monk
- **Support**: Cleric, Druid, Ranger
- **Arcane Corps**: Wizard, Artificer
- **Rare in army**: Sorcerer, Warlock, Rogue

## Formal Institutions

| Institution | Location | Trains |
|-------------|----------|--------|
| **Weaveheart Academy of Arcane Arts** | Weaveheart | Wizards, Sorcerers (supplementary), Bards (supplementary) |
| **Skywatch War College** | Skywatch | Fighters, Paladins, Rangers, strategic officers |
| **Emberforge Engineering Halls** | Emberforge | Artificers |
| **Church Seminaries** | All capitals | Clerics, Paladins (religious education) |
| **Guiding Hand** | Skywatch | Rangers, Rogues (scout path) |

## Informal Training

- **Apprenticeship**: Most common path (blacksmiths teach artificers, veterans teach fighters)
- **Tribal tradition**: Barbarians (four tribes), some Druids
- **Self-taught**: Sorcerers (innate magic forced to be controlled), some Rogues
- **Wandering master**: Monks (rare post-invasion), some Bards
- **Pact-based**: Warlocks (power granted directly by patron  -  no training needed)

## Subclasses as Cultural Traditions

Each subclass is associated with specific institutions or cultural traditions:

- **Wizard specializations**: Evocation (battle-mages), Abjuration (barrier specialists)  -  Weaveheart; Divination (intelligence)  -  Skywatch; Transmutation  -  Emberforge
- **Cleric domains**: Life  -  Order of the Dawn; Forge  -  Guild of the Spark; Nature  -  Circle of the Wild; Twilight  -  Vigil of the Dusk; Trickery  -  Coven of the Spider (secret); Death  -  Order of the Raven (banned)
- **Fighter archetypes**: Battle Master (officers, Skywatch); Champion (rank-and-file); Eldritch Knight (rare, Weaveheart)
- **Paladin oaths**: Devotion  -  Order of the Dawn; Crown  -  Order of the Scales; Vengeance  -  monster-hunters
- **Druid circles**: Land (biome-specific); Moon (frontier); Stars (rare)
- **Ranger conclaves**: Hunter (standard); Gloom Stalker (deep frontier); Beast Master
- **Rogue archetypes**: Thief (ruin-delvers); Scout (Skywatch); Assassin (rare)
- **Barbarian paths**: Berserker (all tribes); Totem Warrior (environmental spirits); Ancestral Guardian (fallen ancestors)

## Class Public Perception Summary

| Class | Perception |
|-------|------------|
| Artificer | Highly respected, valued in Emberforge & frontier |
| Barbarian | Respected warrior tradition, four tribes |
| Bard | Highly respected history-keepers and diplomats |
| Cleric | Pillars of communities, trusted |
| Druid | Respected, essential on frontier |
| Fighter | Backbone of military, common and respected |
| Monk | Rare, viewed with curiosity and respect |
| Paladin | Respected holy warriors, military arm of faith |
| Ranger | Essential for survival, deeply respected |
| Rogue | Feared, distrusted, but essential |
| Sorcerer | Curiosity + mistrust (uncontrolled power) |
| Warlock | Mistrust + fear-respect (unknown entities) |
| Wizard | Respected in Weaveheart, scholarly elite |

## The Adventurers' Guild & Classes

The **Drakh Ix'thar** (Adventurers' Guild) does not restrict membership by class  -  all classes welcome. The guild's internal structure, ranks, and class-specific branches are documented in its own entity file.

**Guild ranks** advance based on successful contracts and contribution to reconquering. Ranks named in Draconic after legendary beasts, highest being **Drah Ix'thari** (Dragon Hunter).
